All of the designs are definitely a step up from the plain white comforters that dominate the market.

Adding both inserts inside a duvet cover can feel heavy and harder to wrangle.

Contributor Yelena Moroz Alpert has had this wool comforter for over two years, and it’s her favorite for cool weather. The bedding is durable with a little heft, and the fill is a breathable medium weight. This is an ideal compromise with her husband since she’s a cold sleeper and he is constantly throwing off covers.

In a recent development, the organic cotton shell makes it feel crisp to the touch, but the wool fill makes it plush on the inside. The comforter makes Alpert’s bed an oasis after tending to her two elementary school-aged kids throughout the day. “Once they are off to bed, all I want to do is burrow in my comforter and read a book,” she claims. “Because I live in a historical brick home, even when the heat is on, the upstairs remains chill, so my bed has to have a lofty layer and I quite truly hibernate under this duvet.”.

Might require steaming to prevent wrinkly appearance.

According to recent reports, even though the brand recommends layering with a duvet for extra coverage, contributor Blake Bakkila always feels tempted to leave this reversible silk comforter on its own to style her bed. “The stitching and two-sided design are versatile and detailed,” she says of the white and grey blanket. The material makeup is even more of a draw. “The silk is naturally temperature-regulating, requires fewer carbon emissions and water usage than cotton products, and is 100% biodegradable,” Bakkila explains. Keep in mind that this feels more like a weighted blanket than a fluffy comforter, like our Brooklinen top pick. It is still lightweight enough for layering without getting too warm, though. In fact, Bakkila says it paired perfectly with her airy, stonewashed linen duvet cover over the summer and helped her sleep comfortably during a heat wave in Southern California.

“Anyone who sleeps hot but still wants plenty of comfort and coverage overnight should definitely invest in this comforter,” she says. “At $399, it’s also fairly priced compared to other comforters I’ve owned, and the eco-friendly materials and manufacturing process will make you feel even better about your purchase.”.

It’s a little heavy to situate inside of a duvet cover.

Industry observers note that as someone who loves switching up their bedding every season but also has a tight storage situation, this adjustable comforter brings Baker the type of bliss she didn’t know existed. It has two panels that can be removed or stacked on top of each other, which is especially helpful for co-sleeping. The cover is cushy from the squishy microfiber inner fill, but it also feels polished because of the cotton sateen shell. This is one of Baker’s favorites since she can easily customize the panels, but she actually praises it year-round because it’s more breathable than those synthetic comforters that claim otherworldly cooling capabilities. Her cashmere duvet cover is a mainstay on her bed these days, and she says the comforter stills feels well-ventilated.

Recent findings suggest that “Now that it’s safe to say it’ll be cold here until April, I’ve been using the double panels on my bed for extra warmth,” Baker notes. “It almost feels like a gentle weighted blanket easing me to sleep each night.” The wooden buttons on the comforter look like the ones on her winter sweaters, and their delicate and durable designs keep the panels from budging.

What Is the Difference Between a Comforter and a Duvet Insert?

According to recent reports, A comforter is a single, often quilted, piece of bedding with a fabric cover encasing the plush fill in between the two fabric layers. A duvet, on the other hand, refers to both the insert and fabric cover. A comforter can be colorful or white, and made in a variety of fabrics. The fabric cover of a comforter is stitched directly onto the fill (down, feathers, or polyester are most common). A duvet’s cover is removable, and often tied to the corners via loops attached to the insert.

Recent findings suggest that not necessarily. Many duvet inserts are designed to be used on their own, as a comforter, or with a cover. I recommend a cover to help protect your duvet insert, ensure it lasts as long as possible, and make laundry day as easy as possible. Duvet covers act as a protective layer, keeping sweat, body oils, and normal wear from affecting your duvet insert. Plus, duvet covers allow you to add personality to your bedscape, whether you prefer an all-white minimalist look or a maximalist ruffle.

What Is the Best Type of Filling for a Duvet?

Similar to quality, the “best” filling is pretty subjective. People often choose silk, lyocell, down, or down-alternative fills. Down comforters tend to be firmer and heavier, while down-alternatives are usually considered more lightweight and airy. Down-alternatives derive from recycled and allergen-friendly materials, so they’re ideal for people who prefer or require those types of fillings. The fill power will also determine the ultimate comfort level, and most should hover around 650 for a plush, down-like feel.

And again, those care instructions come into play. If you’d rather throw your comforter in the wash, that’s most down comforters in our list can handle it. Meanwhile, some specialty down-alternatives (like bamboo viscose options) need to take a trip to the dry cleaners, which can make them higher maintenance and more expensive long-term.

Does the Quality of a Duvet Insert Matter?

In terms of “quality,” you’ll see the effects in two main areas: the price point and longevity of your duvet insert. For instance, a down comforter with 750 fill power like Brooklinen’s heavyweight comforter is specifically designed for keeping you warm during colder winter months (or for anyone who spends most nights shivering). The fill power makes it lofty and fluffy, but the construction can also keep it lofty and fluffy.

It has been revealed that baffle-box construction, as mentioned above, is also considered a higher quality design option, which holds fill in separate chambers to keep the fill even. All of this mentioned, the most expensive, technically high-quality comforters aren’t necessarily the best for every type of sleeper. And while we love comforters and duvet inserts that run as high as $500, we’ve also scoured the internet and tested alternatives you can shop for less than $100 on Amazon (we’re looking at you, Bedsure Waffle Comforter Set).

It’s also notable to keep in mind that your duvet insert’s quality depends on how you care for it. Make sure to carefully read the care instructions, and if needed, take it to a trustworthy dry cleaner for a gentle clean (experts say about two to three times per year).

How Do You Put a Duvet Cover on an Insert or Comforter?

Follow these steps from Monelle Totah, cofounder of Hudson Grace, for a lump-free way to put an insert or comforter inside a duvet cover:.

How Do I Wash a Duvet Insert/Comforter?

In a recent development, it’s important to always check your specific product’s care instructions before washing. For example, the Buffy Breeze duvet insert recommends a spot clean or dry clean only, while the Boll & Branch comforter is machine washable on a gentle cycle. To take out the guesswork, we’ve included the product’s care instructions right above each of our review descriptions.

Industry observers note that diana Ciechorska, general manager at Park Slope Cleaning, a commercial cleaning company in Upcoming York City, claims the standard first step for washing your comforter includes treating any visible stains before you load the comforter into the washing machine. “Opt for a gentle cycle with cold water, using a mild detergent,” she says. “An extra rinse cycle ensures no detergent residue remains.”.

Recent findings suggest that when taking a comforter out of the dryer, Parima Ijaz, the Fresh Jersey–based founder of bedding line Pure Parima, recommends holding the corners to shake and fluff it. This allows the fill to distribute even after being jumbled up in the dryer. If possible, she indicates it’s ideal to let the comforter air-dry for an extra day to make sure it is completely dry before dressing your bed.

How Often Should You Wash Your Comforter?

Comforters and duvet inserts accumulate “dust, sweat, and oils, which can cause allergies and wear down the fabric,” notes Camden Olivero, COO and cofounder of Clotheslyne, an on-demand pick-up and delivery laundry service. With this in mind, I recommend washing your comforter two to three times a year to help keep allergens at bay and the covering in its best condition (double check the label first, though).

How Should You Store a Comforter?

Like your other linens, it’s best to keep your comforter in a cool, dry place to avoid mold or moisture buildup. Keep the comforter out of plastic and cedar too, as these materials can cause yellowing.

How Do You Dispose of Old Comforters?

In a recent development, if your old comforter is still in good condition, we recommend donating it to charities in your area. However, if you’re looking to purely dispose of old comforters, organizations like Trashie ethically recycle textiles for you to keep them out of landfills—so long as they’re clean and free of soil like motor oil or paint.

What Kind of Duvet Inserts Do Hotels Use?

In a recent development, if you want to mimic your latest hotel stay at home, you’re not alone. We’ve reviewed the best hotel comforters, which are often sold on luxury hotel chain websites like Marriott and Four Seasons. There are several getaways that use Frette’s bedding, too, including The Palace Hotel in Madrid. In most hotel duvet inserts, there are a few common traits: decadent down or hypoallergenic, plant-based down-alternative fills; high fill powers, around 800; organic cotton or bamboo viscose covers for breathability; and carefully designed baffle-box or box-stitch construction to keep fill in place and make it last.

Are Duvet Inserts Machine Washable?

Industry observers note that fortunately, most of our favorite duvet inserts are machine washable and can even go in the dryer. Some will require a commercial washer (especially if they’re bulky), though, and others like the comforters from Quince and Cozy Earth should take a trip to the dry cleaners. Read the care label, and see what’s best for your duvet insert.

According to recent reports, ijaz recommends washing your comforter in a front-loading washing machine since an upright machine is too abrasive. “Using a top loader with a spindle in the middle can damage the comforter and make it harder to properly and evenly wash it,” she says. Otherwise, her general suggestions are like what the experts noted in this story: Wash your comforter on a cold, gentle cycle and avoid harsh softeners and chemicals so the shell and fill stay in the best condition.

How Do I Choose the Right Duvet Insert for Different Seasons?

Sources indicate that there are duvet inserts and comforters with heavy fill powers (think 800 and above) for harsh winter months or cold sleepers, lightweight options (400 or below) for summer months or hot sleepers, and medium weights (around 400 to 600) for year-round comfort. We’ve also learned that the fluffiest duvet inserts often give sleepers that Goldilocks-level sleep. “A fluffy, high-loft duvet delivers the most consistent sleep experience across seasons,” Anthony Loiacono, director of rooms at L’Auberge de Sedona, previously told AD. “It provides warmth without weight, and most importantly, adapts to day-to-night temperature shifts.” Frette’s Cortina Medium Down Duvet Filler has all-season appeal, and you can always layer with an extra blanket if you want more coverage on colder nights.

It has been revealed that not all duvet inserts are created equal. This is a lesson you learn early on, when you wake up either sweating or freezing in the middle of the night. The fact is that this annoying experience is also completely avoidable. Reading up on the duvet insert you're considering buying—and actually understanding what all the terms mean—will tell you everything you need to know, including how hot it’s going to be and whether or not the down is going to end up smooshed in one corner come morning. So, I put this guide together with the help of Danielle Trotter, the textiles technical designer at West Elm, to break down what to consider in the confusing world that is duvet insert fillings, fill power, and the different types of construction.

Fill Power: This is the measurement of how much down occupies a cubic inch of space in the insert, a.k.a. how “lofty” it feels. You’ll usually see numbers in the 500s and up. The higher the fill power, the fluffier and warmer it will feel. I typically like fill powers that hover around 800 during the colder months. This fill power is typically on the marshmallowy side of the spectrum and feels cozier and insulating when the temperature outside starts to drop. For the summertime, 600 fill power or so is usually a sweet spot for me since it’s more airy and breathable, but individual preferences may vary.

Corner Loops: If there are corner loops or anchor loops, that means you can use the comforter as a duvet insert. If there are no loops, the comforter might be prone to clumping and bunching within the duvet, so we wouldn’t recommend it unless you have a lot of patience. Some of the loops in this list reach up to 12, which are super helpful to keep the fill even.

Fill Content: Fill material is usually classified as either down or down alternative options.

It has been revealed that outer Shell: The material on the outer shell of your comforter or duvet insert matters. Look at the thread count. I find that fabrics with thread counts around 300 are typically soft and airy. Consider your preferred sleeping temperature and whether a cotton sateen shell that’s smooth but slightly thicker is a better option than one made of crisp percale cotton. If you’re a hot sleeper, you’ll probably want a cooling material with breathability, like eucalyptus.

In a recent development, size and Color: The size of your insert is dictated by the size of your bed. Companies usually offer all standard sizes from twin to king, with some brands offering California king as well. In terms of color, white is most popular for the duvet insert, but you can also find ivory relatively easily. Comforter color ranges are more expansive, and you can likely find a hue that fits your decor. I’ve called out what’s available in each of the product picks.

Thread Count: This is the number of horizontal and vertical threads per square inch of the duvet insert's outer fabric. Expert tip: “In theory, people think that the higher the thread count, the better the quality because more yarns are being used,” Trotter states. “However, it’s the quality of the yarns or even the type of weave that really matters!”.

Recent findings suggest that baffle-Box Construction: This design means the comforter or duvet insert has sewn-in square chambers with side walls. “Each chamber has an equal amount of fill, and the side walls prevent the fill from shifting,” says Trotter. “This construction is considered to be of a better quality because warmth is evenly distributed.”.

Recent findings suggest that sewn-Through Construction: This type of construction is when the duvet insert is made of two pieces of fabric sewn around the perimeter, then filled and quilted into squares. This means the top and bottom of the comforter are sewn together. In turn, the fill is shift- and bunch-resistant. While this is a great option for those who like low-maintenance laundry days since you can typically toss these comforter types in the washing machine, the tighter construction usually makes the fill less lofty. Plus, cold air can seep through the seams, so it’s more ideal for a summer bedscape.

Hyundai is skipping the typical mid-cycle refresh and plans to launch a completely redesigned Kona, with a sleek new style and an updated high-tech interior.

While earlier reports suggested Hyundai planned to drop the all-electric Kona variant and would only offer gas and hybrid versions, the prototype captured in Korea is expected to be the EV model. However, Hyundai has yet to confirm powertrain or battery specs.

In a recent development, the updates are even more evident on the inside. Previous spy images appeared to show the third-gen Hyundai Kona running Hyundai’s latest Pleos Connect infotainment system, like the IONIQ 3.

In the IONIQ 3, Hyundai offers a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen, plus an optional driver display.

Like the current model, the third-gen Kona is expected to be available with fully electric (EV), hybrid, and gas-powered powertrains.

While Hyundai skipped the 2026 Kona EV, the electric version could return in 2027 or 2028 when the third-generation model is expected to arrive.

The hybrid version will likely use the same 1.6L hybrid engine as the upcoming Seltos, while the EV variant could offer similar powertrain and battery options to the IONIQ 3.

The IONIQ 3 is available with two battery packs in Europe and the UK: 42 kWh and 61 kWh, offering WLTP ranges of up to 213 miles (344 km) and 308 miles (497 km), respectively.

Christina Applegate ‘Not Happy at All’ After Learning She Was Misdiagnosed With MS

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1008 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Christina Applegate shared an unexpected health revision on her return to the MeSsy podcast with co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler.
  • The two actors have detailed their experiences with multiple sclerosis (MS), a neurological disorder that can lead to debilitating symptoms affecting daily functioning and quality of life.
  • Applegate, 54, has been raising awareness about the condition since her initial diagnosis in 2021.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christina Applegate shared an unexpected health revision on her return to the MeSsy podcast with co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler.

The two actors have detailed their experiences with multiple sclerosis (MS), a neurological disorder that can lead to debilitating symptoms affecting daily functioning and quality of life.

Applegate, 54, has been raising awareness about the condition since her initial diagnosis in 2021.

In two podcast episodes released October 20, Applegate revealed that doctors had told her she was misdiagnosed with MS.

Industry observers note that “She came into my room and stated, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS,’ ” Applegate said as she fought back tears. “I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy.”.

The “Anchorman” and “Dead to Me” actor explained that her symptoms have continued to worsen, leaving her without an explanation for what she’s experiencing as doctors investigate the cause.

Industry observers note that being misdiagnosed with MS is relatively common. Applegate’s revelation highlights a difficult reality for people living with unexplained symptoms resembling MS. Her experience raises questions about how MS is diagnosed, why misdiagnoses may occur, and what people can do when their symptoms don’t match their diagnosis.

It has been revealed that while MS can be difficult to diagnose, an accurate diagnosis can help people with the condition gain access to appropriate treatment. A misdiagnosis, on the other hand, may lead to unnecessary interventions and medication, and take an emotional toll over time.

“MS can be challenging to diagnose because there is no single test that confirms it in every case,” said Steve Allder, MD, consultant neurologist at Re:Cognition Health.

Sources indicate that “An incorrect diagnosis can have significant consequences. Someone incorrectly diagnosed with MS may experience considerable anxiety, undergo unnecessary investigations, or receive treatments with potential risks and side effects. Equally, if MS is missed, treatment may be delayed, potentially allowing further neurological damage,” Allder told Healthline.

A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis underscores that MS misdiagnoses remain a concern.

Research suggests that around 15% of people diagnosed with MS may actually have another condition.

However, estimates vary across studies, with some reporting rates ranging from 5–41%.

While an accurate diagnosis can guide patients toward appropriate treatment, a mistaken one may lead to unnecessary medication, emotional distress, and years of uncertainty.

Fresh diagnostic guidelines offer hope for greater accuracy, but they also raise important questions about how doctors can adequately distinguish MS from other conditions.

“Research has shown that MS can be both overdiagnosed and underdiagnosed,” Allder stated.

In a recent development, “Diagnosis relies on a combination of symptoms, neurological examination, MRI findings, and sometimes, additional tests. It is also key to recognize that diagnoses can evolve as new evidence emerges. As neurologists, we must remain open to revisiting a diagnosis when symptoms or test results do not fit, ensuring patients receive appropriate treatment and support.”.

MS symptoms may vary widely and overlap with several other conditions. These may include:.

Because these conditions share certain features with MS, healthcare professionals should consider a patient’s full clinical profile rather than relying on a single symptom or scan.

Sources indicate that “MS can cause numbness, tingling, muscle weakness, visual disturbances, balance problems, and fatigue. However, these symptoms are not unique to the condition,” Allder mentioned.

“For example, numbness and tingling may indicate peripheral neuropathy, sometimes associated with diabetes or vitamin B12 deficiency. Weakness or altered sensation may result from a trapped nerve or spinal cord compression. Migraines can cause visual disturbances and sensory symptoms, while inner-ear disorders may affect balance,” he continued.

Allder noted that fatigue is particularly nonspecific and may be associated with:.

He explained that, as a neurologist, he considers the pattern, duration, and progression of symptoms alongside examination findings.

Recent findings suggest that “No single symptom automatically indicates MS. A thorough assessment is essential to identify the underlying cause and ensure the patient receives appropriate treatment,” he stated.

There is no single test that definitively confirms every case of MS.

Diagnosis typically involves reviewing symptoms, conducting neurological examinations, and evaluating MRI scans and laboratory results.

MRI findings may be tricky to interpret. Some white-matter spots resemble MS lesions but may result from migraine, aging, or other conditions. Misapplying diagnostic criteria or overlooking alternative explanations can also lead to mistakes.

“MRI abnormalities alone do not confirm MS,” Allder noted. “The diagnosis must be based on the overall clinical picture, with alternative explanations carefully considered.”.

Research also suggests that MS misdiagnosis rates may differ by sex.

Research highlights females are 2.1 times more likely to be misdiagnosed with MS than males, highlighting the potential for diagnostic bias and differences in how symptoms are evaluated.

The updated MS diagnostic criteria published in 2025 offer a framework for improving diagnosis.

The updated guidelines introduce several notable changes.

For instance, the optic nerve (the nerve connecting the eye to the brain) is now included as a fifth anatomical location for assessing evidence of MS.

The revised criteria also include new MRI biomarkers, such as the central vein sign and paramagnetic rim lesions. These features can help doctors distinguish MS-related abnormalities from other conditions.

These changes may help doctors diagnose MS earlier and more accurately.

It has been revealed that if you experience persistent or recurring neurological symptoms, seek medical advice. Your doctor can assess your symptoms and, if applicable, refer you to a neurologist.

Sudden weakness, vision loss, or difficulty speaking requires urgent medical assessment, Allder stated.

“Depending on the findings, investigations may include MRI scans of the brain and spinal cord, blood tests, and, in some cases, a lumbar puncture,” Allder noted.

“It is important that results are interpreted alongside symptoms and examination findings, as no single test should determine the diagnosis in isolation.”.

Allder remarked that if you’re unsure about a diagnosis, you can ask your neurologist what evidence supports it and whether alternative health conditions have been considered.

In a recent development, “A second opinion or follow-up assessment may be appropriate. The priority is an accurate diagnosis that leads to the right treatment and support,” Allder noted.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.
  • The Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected.
  • Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator indicates today with a Los Angeles delivery address:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.

The Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected. So the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today costs $109,990, up 57% from $69,990 in early August.

Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator indicates today with a Los Angeles delivery address:.

According to recent reports, A week ago, the Cyberbeast cost $102,490. Before that, it was $99,990. That’s a $10,000 (10%) increase in about a week on a truck that hasn’t changed: 320 miles of estimated range, 11,000 lbs of towing, and 0-60 mph in 2.6 seconds.

Sources indicate that on November 6, the same day Elon Musk announced the end of Cybertruck production, Tesla raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and paused orders for the base Dual Motor. That made the $92,490 Premium AWD the entry point. Now it’s gone too, with no announcement. The configurator just stopped letting you pick it.

According to recent reports, upcoming inventory isn’t an alternative either. When we checked, Tesla’s inventory search revealed no new Cybertrucks within 200 miles of Los Angeles.

This comes two days after Musk extended Cybertruck production through the end of summer 2027 to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” On Monday, he claimed the order rate “far exceeds” production and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.”.

Sources indicate that if there really is a backlog, cutting off the two cheaper trims is one way to cap it before the line shuts down. It also pushes whatever demand is left toward the most expensive, highest-margin version of the truck.

Industry observers note that but the sales data doesn’t describe a truck with a demand problem in the other direction. We estimate Tesla delivered 7,000 to 8,000 Cybertrucks in Q3, a pace of about 30,000 a year on a line with more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. And in February, Tesla was offering a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 for “only the next 10 days.”.

That’s $50,000 less than the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today. Nine months later.

Some of those $59,990 buyers are still waiting on delivery dates pushed into 2027. Tesla hasn’t said whether their orders, or any other Dual Motor and Premium orders in the queue, will be built before production ends.

Unlike the thousands of $59k CT orders that may never get manufactured I can guarantee that every high margin $110k CyberBeast order will be delivered before production ends.

Recent findings suggest that this is the wind-down playbook, and it’s moving faster than I expected. Announce the end, raise prices, pull the cheaper trims, and sell the last trucks in their most expensive form. Tesla is squeezing as much as it can out of every remaining Cybertruck.

Industry observers note that I don’t blame Tesla for wanting margin on a program it’s walking away from. But it makes the “order backlog” talk look like what we noted it was: an end-of-life rush Tesla created by announcing the end, now being monetized with a $109,990 sticker. Not great for anyone who was told in 2019 that this truck would start at $39,900, or that the tri-motor version would cost $69,900.

According to recent reports, if you want a Cybertruck that isn’t a Cyberbeast, you’re now shopping used. And I’d keep an eye on used prices, because a truck that’s going out of production with no cheaper latest option could hold its value better than it has over the last two years.

Latest Update: A New Gut-Brain Pathway That May Affect Your Mood

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1165 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • “Tiny bubbles in the mind, make me feel happy, make me feel fine.”—with apologies to Don Ho.
  • For the last decade or so, scientists have been aware of at least three ways that microbes can communicate with our brain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

“Tiny bubbles in the mind, make me feel happy, make me feel fine.”—with apologies to Don Ho.

For the last decade or so, scientists have been aware of at least three ways that microbes can communicate with our brain. One is hormones, including the stress hormone cortisol. Another is through the vagus nerve that connects the gut to the brain. And the third is the immune system that constantly tracks microbes and their secretions. But a fourth method has slowly come to light: extracellular vesicles (EVs). These are tiny bubbles that bud off of bacteria and can travel seemingly everywhere through the body.

EVs have been known about for decades, although exactly what they are and what they do has been a little fuzzy. In 1967, Peter Wolf described particles that separated out with high-speed centrifugation of blood, which he called “platelet dust." In 1983, Rose Johnstone found EVs in immature red blood cells by serendipity. She called it an “Alice in Blunderland” discovery.

Since then, EVs have been found everywhere we look, in all kingdoms of life, including bacteria, fungi, plants, and animals. At first, it seemed like cells were producing the EVs as little trash bags. But more recent research has found that EVs are far more complex, carrying everything from proteins, microRNA, DNA, neurotransmitters, anti-tumor peptides, and even cellular organelles like mitochondria. They provide interkingdom communication, acting as messengers, repair modules, and yes, trash bags.

Their membranes are studded with proteins that serve as addresses, directing them to specific tissues where they can latch on and spill their contents. That mechanism is exciting to researchers who are starting to create EVs that can aim therapies at specific tissues.

They are small enough to pass right through an intact gut lining where they can enter the bloodstream. Some bacterial EVs can slip directly into our cells, which is usually not a good thing. Fortunately, most of those are summarily captured and dissolved on the spot. Surprisingly, EVs can also pass through the blood-brain barrier to send messages deep into the brain. That may be good or bad, depending on their origin.

A recent Korean study by Se-Young Choi and colleagues found that EVs released by Fusobacterium nucleatum contributed to neuroinflammation and caused anxiety and depression when injected into the brains of mice. The EVs acted to shift neurons from excitatory to inhibitory, likely explaining the low energy and listlessness of the affected mice. Although mice love to sip sugar, these mice couldn’t be bothered to leave their nest. This is classic sickness behavior, surprisingly similar to depression. The EVs also stimulated the brain’s immune cells, called microglia.

Industry observers note that an earlier Korean study by Juli Choi and colleagues used an in vitro analysis to observe the effects of the probiotic Lactiplantibacillus plantarum. They started by stressing mouse hippocampal cells with the stress hormone corticosterone. This had the predicted effect of lowering expression of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), which helps neurons to survive and grow and is associated with improved learning and memory.

When they added EVs from L. plantarum, BDNF levels were restored. They found the same thing in living mice that were exposed to stress: Their BDNF levels dropped and were restored with injections of L. plantarum EVs. Here, the injections were into the gut of the mice, not directly into the brain, demonstrating that EVs are likely traveling from the gut to the brain, sailing through the blood-brain barrier.

Similar results have been found in different studies for Lactobacillus paracasei, Akkermansia muciniphila, Bacteroides fragilis, and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus. They each have multiple methods of action, including butyrate production, tryptophan metabolism, and quelling inflammation.

That makes these important microbes psychobiotics: bacteria that can improve mood. The effect of these EVs is consequential: In some cases, they work as well as antidepressants.

Mice are the perfect animals for this research, as their plumbing is similar to humans. But mouse bacteria and human bacteria are different, even if there is a family resemblance. In general, the basic principles are conserved, but human studies are necessary before we can take advantage of this amazing science.

Fortunately, the human studies are starting to yield similar results. A review by Kuanjun He and colleagues describes dozens of studies linking bacterial EVs to schizophrenia, bipolar disease, and major depressive disorder.

Recent findings suggest that we have long known that microbes can produce neurotransmitters like dopamine, serotonin, and GABA, all of which are favored targets of psychoactive medicines. But these molecules are excluded by the blood-brain barrier. That is why we don’t simply prescribe serotonin; it won’t pass the barrier. Instead, researchers create serotonin reuptake inhibitors that can enter the brain easily and, once there, can act to increase levels of serotonin in the brain.

According to recent reports, but packaging these molecules into an EV lets them slide right into the brain. At some point, it is likely that formulators will take advantage of this packaging trick to get previously excluded drugs into the brain.

According to recent reports, the truly exciting news here is that you can put EVs to work for you today. Start by avoiding the junk food that is destroying your gut microbes, and switch to something like a plant-heavy Mediterranean diet with lots of variety. Ecologically, diversity is a winning strategy for a harmonious microbiome. With a bounty of different microbes, it is difficult for a small number of bully species to dominate.

Industry observers note that intriguingly, the food you eat is also full of EVs. Natural foods like milk, grapes, broccoli, and ginger are packed with EVs that escape digestion and can slip directly into your bloodstream. Once there, they can change the way your stress genes are expressed, improve insulin sensitivity, and lower inflammation. These happy bubbles may be tiny, but they are potent.

Industry observers note that chung, Chaelin, Young Lee, Hyun Young Kim, et al. “Extracellular Vesicles of Fusobacterium Nucleatum Induce Anxiety and Depression by Triggering Neuroinflammation via IL-1β.” Journal of Neuroinflammation, ahead of print, November 11, 2026. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12974-026-04107-4.

Choi, Juli, Yoon-Keun Kim, and Pyung-Lim Han. “Extracellular Vesicles Derived from Lactobacillus Plantarum Increase BDNF Expression in Cultured Hippocampal Neurons and Produce Antidepressant-like Effects in Mice.” Experimental Neurobiology 28, no. 2 (2019): 158–71. https://doi.org/10.5607/en.2019.28.2.158.

According to recent reports, cai, Saijun, Zhen Hu, Xianzhe Ma, and Jinghao Sheng. “Bacterial Extracellular Vesicles in the Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis: Biogenesis, Cargo, Delivery, and Neuromodulatory Functions.” Extracellular Vesicles and Circulating Nucleic Acids 7, no. 4 (2026): 1825–41. https://doi.org/10.20517/evcna.2026.94.

Kaisanlahti, Anna, Sonja Salmi, Sohvi Kumpula, et al. “Bacterial Extracellular Vesicles – Brain Invaders? A Systematic Review.” Frontiers in Molecular Neuroscience 16 (September 2023). https://doi.org/10.3389/fnmol.2023.1227655.

According to recent reports, guo, Chuang, Yulong Bai, Pengfei Li, and Kuanjun He. “The Emerging Roles of Microbiota-Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Psychiatric Disorders.” Frontiers in Microbiology 15 (April 2024). https://doi.org/10.3389/fmicb.2024.1383199.

Latest Update: RFK Jr.’s Revised Vaccine Schedule May Cause 83% Surge in Hepatitis B Infections

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F.
  • Concerns include a rise in preventable infectious diseases such as measles, polio, and hepatitis B.
  • A new study suggests that delaying or foregoing the hepatitis B shot for newborns could increase chronic infections among children.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s proposed changes to the childhood vaccine schedule have raised alarm among public health experts and researchers.

Concerns include a rise in preventable infectious diseases such as measles, polio, and hepatitis B.

A new study suggests that delaying or foregoing the hepatitis B shot for newborns could increase chronic infections among children.

In December 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) ended its recommendation for universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth for infants whose mothers test negative for the virus. Instead, the federal health agency recommends individual-based clinical decision making.

After reviewing the evidence, the CDC, which is overseen by the HHS, concluded that newborns “face little risk of contracting hepatitis,” which deemed the vaccine, typically administered at birth, unnecessary.

Experts say this shift in public health policy wasn’t based on science, and researchers warn of rising infection rates.

“Hepatitis B immunizations have been proven to protect individuals against a serious and significant disease,” mentioned Graham Tse, MD, pediatrician and chief medical officer of MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, CA.

Sources indicate that “The hepatitis B vaccines have several decades of history and have been proven safe and effective,” Tse stated. “There has been no new data or evidence presented or uncovered to support delaying the newborn dose of hepatitis B.”.

Here’s what parents should know about making informed decisions with their child’s healthcare team.

A U.S. modeling study published in Annals of Internal Medicine on October 20 projected that delaying the first vaccine dose until 2 months could increase chronic hepatitis B infections among infants by 19% under one scenario.

With shared decision making and lower vaccine uptake, projected increases ranged from 83% to 225%, compared with universal birth-dose vaccination.

The researchers also estimated that up to 1.8 million young adults could remain susceptible to hepatitis B by age 20 under shared decision making, compared with 232,000 under universal birth dosing.

Another study published in JAMA Pediatrics in late April projected hundreds of additional chronic infections annually if the hepatitis B birth dose were delayed or omitted.

Recent findings suggest that however, these figures are model-based projections, rather than verified outcomes. Actual results will depend on vaccination rates and other factors.

In December 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) adopted a recommendation shifting away from universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth for infants whose mothers test negative for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg).

Under the upcoming approach, parents and healthcare professionals can decide together whether to give the first dose at birth or defer it until the baby is 2 months old.

Sources indicate that the change followed an 8 to 3 vote by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), marking a departure from longstanding U.S. guidance.

However, infants born to mothers who test positive for hepatitis B or whose infection status is unknown should still receive the hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) within 12 hours of birth, according to the updated guidelines.

Hepatitis B is a viral infection that affects the liver.

Although some infections resolve, newborns and infants face a higher risk of developing lifelong hepatitis B infection compared with adults.

Up to 90% of infants infected during their first year develop chronic hepatitis B.

“We have actual world evidence that vaccinating newborns for hepatitis B prevents hepatitis B infections later in life and the serious complications of that disease,” Tse remarked.

Over time, chronic infection can lead to cirrhosis, liver failure, or liver cancer.

“The danger of delaying the newborn hepatitis B shot is that individuals do not get vaccinated and thereby do not have protection against hepatitis B,” Tse said.

Early vaccination helps protect young infants before potential exposure occurs, including situations in which maternal screening misses an infection.

“Newborns can be infected with hepatitis B from a mother who is not aware they have a hepatitis B infection or from exposure later in life,” Tse said.

“The risk is developing a hepatitis B infection, which can potentially lead to liver cancer, fulminant hepatitis, or severe end-stage liver disease.”.

In contrast to the CDC, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) still recommends a universal hepatitis B vaccine dose within 24 hours of birth, followed by additional doses during infancy.

The leading pediatric medical organization has raised concerns about the potential consequences of reduced vaccination rates.

The hepatitis B vaccine has decades of safety and effectiveness data.

Tse mentioned the AAP’s vaccine schedule and recommendations are based on decades of study, use, and expert input, and provide the best protection against vaccine-preventable diseases.

Parents who have questions about potential side effects, timing, or their baby’s individual risk should discuss them with a qualified healthcare professional.

“Parents are confused, given the recommendations from CDC, HHS, and Kennedy differ from established and respected groups such as the American Academy of Pediatrics, the Infectious Disease Society of America, and several states,” Tse remarked.

“Parents desire to keep their children safe, and having differing opinions and confusion will lead to reduced vaccination rates as parents experience doubt as to whom to listen to or believe.”.

While the updated CDC policy offers more flexibility for some families, lower vaccination uptake could lead to an increase in chronic hepatitis B infections.

Ask your pediatrician about the benefits of vaccination against hepatitis B at birth, the risks of delaying the first dose, and the recommended schedule for completing the series.

You can also ask how maternal screening results affect your baby’s protection.

An informed conversation with your healthcare professional can help you weigh the evidence and choose a vaccination initiative for your baby.

“I see no argument whatsoever for changing the established vaccination schedule for hepatitis B,” Tse noted.

“There have been no newly introduced studies, no data, nor evidence to justify Kennedy’s proposed changes to the childhood immunization schedule. Delaying vaccinations or skipping vaccinations puts your child at risk for serious and significant diseases, which are all preventable,” Tse said.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.

As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.

“We simply can’t afford this work right now,” Schäfer mentioned in the memo reviewed by Reuters. The Wolfsburg plant, AKA the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.

Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer revealed earlier this year that the long-awaited electric car was delayed until closer to 2030.

Schäfer suggested the delay was because the SSP (Scalable Systems Platform), which is being developed through its partnership with Rivian, was taking longer than expected, again due to costs.

According to Autocar, Volkswagen is now delaying the Audi A4 E-tron as well, another vehicle that was initially planned to be among the first based on the SSP platform.

Production of the electric A4 is being pushed back until at least 2029, a year later than originally planned. While the delay is disappointing for Audi fans (including myself) still waiting for an electric A4, it also puts Audi behind rival luxury brands in the mid-size sedan segment.

BMW has the new i3, and Mercedes-Benz has the C-Class EV, both of which feature major improvements in range, charging, and efficiency over their previous-generation EVs.

Volkswagen mentioned in 2023 that the 800V SSP will serve as a “single future backbone with integrated electric and electronics architecture,” claiming that more than 40 million models were expected to be built on it.

The company also mentioned investment and R&D costs were expected to be reduced by about 30% compared to the current MEB platform, enabling most models “to achieve the same margin compared to their conventionally powered counterparts.”.

Volkswagen’s software struggles started in its internal division, Cariad, leading to delays, missed targets, and budget overruns.

To fix it, VW turned to Rivian, forming a joint venture to develop its next-gen software-defined vehicle (SDV) electrical architecture.

In March, VW said several test vehicles, including the ID.EVERY1, Audi, and Scout with the SDV architecture underwent “comprehensive evaluation,” and successfully validated over-the-air (OTA) functionality.

Being cash efficient is good, but delays to the next-gen platform that will keep you competitive with rival brands seem like a problem.

However, the Audi A4 E-tron delay is not entirely about software. The Autocar report claims Audi demanded significant changes to the SSP platform for the A4 E-tron so it more closely matched the current gas version.

Audi reportedly wanted individual footwells for front and rear passengers, which would require repositioning the battery.

The luxury brand also reportedly asked for a 48V electrical system instead of the traditional 12V setup initially planned.

While development of the Golf EV is on hold, VW’s works council noted the pause will not delay its launch, promising to make up for lost time. It’s still expected to launch in 2030. The Audi A4 E-tron is now expected to arrive around 2029.

Recent findings suggest that while a few games have broken their launch Steam player records in the past, it’s incredibly rare to see it happen - especially twice in such a short period after launch. Embark clearly has a winner on its hands here.

Industry observers note that arc Raiders’ next big moment is the game’s first post-launch map, which is set to arrive at some point this month, alongside newly introduced Quests and other gameplay items. Seeing as how the Steam concurrent record has been broken twice, there’s every chance the arrival of the new map will bring another boost to player numbers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in a new analysis, researchers found females with endometriosis were 2.3 times more likely to also have migraine, and they said the two conditions may share a pain pathway involving nerves and inflammation.Recognizing that connection earlier could lead to coordinated care for both conditions, the researchers said.The analysis, presented at the American Neurological Association (ANA) Annual Meeting in San Diego on October 20, included more than 13 million females. The research hasn’t yet been published in a peer-reviewed scientific journal.

Endometriosis occurs when tissue similar to what lines the uterus grows outside the uterus, Mallory Stuparich, MD, a gynecologic surgeon at MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, California, told Healthline. Stuparich was not involved in the study.Yohannes Woubishet Woldeamanuel, MD, lead author of the study and assistant professor of neurology at Mayo Clinic Arizona, told Healthline that migraine also involves more than one part of the body.“Migraine is more than a headache,” he remarked.Headache is one symptom, Woldeamanuel said, but migraine can also cause sensory, motor, and balance symptoms.“Migraine is a little complex. It’s a multiple-nervous system involving a condition,” he said.

Stuparich said endometriosis pain typically develops in 2 ways. The first starts in the lesions themselves.“There are inflammatory markers that are created by the endometriosis lesions themselves, and those inflammatory markers can irritate the nerves that live close by the lesions,” she said.The second involves the nervous system, Stuparich said. Scar tissue can grow its own nerve supply, and years of chronic pain can change how the nervous system responds. That adaptation can “perpetuate pain or make people feel sensations that normally wouldn’t be painful,” she said.Stuparich said the inflammatory and immune processes involved in endometriosis have “pretty significant overlap in the setting of migraines.”.

Industry observers note that one possible link between the two conditions is calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), a chemical messenger that helps transmit pain signals, the researchers noted.CGRP plays a key role in migraine attacks, Woldeamanuel said, and blocking it reduces those attacks. CGRP medications work by blocking the sites where CGRP attaches or by binding to CGRP itself.Researchers have also found CGRP in endometriosis tissue.

A 2024 study published in Science Translational Medicine found CGRP in endometriosis lesions from both people and mice. In mice, blocking CGRP signaling reduced pain and reduced lesion size.

Other studies point to shared biology between the two conditions:.

It has been revealed that stuparich remarked she was “not surprised at all” by the finding because it matches what she sees in her own patients.“We see this overlap of patients who have endometriosis also having migraines,” she said.Stuparich said the science still has gaps. She noted that nothing has been proven conclusively in peer-reviewed research yet, but the way both diseases behave supports a connection.“It makes sense that there would be overlap,” she said.

Endometriosis and migraine are treated by different specialists, so the overlap is easy to miss, Woldeamanuel stated.For the analysis, researchers at Mayo Clinic Arizona reviewed 35 studies published over 50 years, comparing migraine rates among 207,675 females with endometriosis and 12,963,120 females without the condition.Short-term health records miss up to 90% of that overlap, according to the analysis. Migraine rates in females with endometriosis changed depending on how each study identified migraine.“This data is hiding,” Woldeamanuel said.

Industry observers note that “These two clinics are siloed. One clinic doesn’t ask about the other condition. They just focus on their own specialty,” Woldeamanuel said.The findings of the analysis have not been published in a peer-reviewed journal.

It has been revealed that some treatments already overlap, Stuparich stated. Hormonal birth control “can sometimes be used to treat menstrually associated migraines,” she said.Stuparich said she has heard anecdotally of patients whose endometriosis symptoms improved after they started CGRP medications for migraine, though long-term data are still lacking.The researchers said the findings support studying whether existing CGRP-blocking migraine medications could also relieve endometriosis pain, potentially offering one treatment for both conditions.Woldeamanuel leads a planned Mayo Clinic trial testing one of those medications, rimegepant (Nurtec ODT), for endometriosis pain. The trial will also track migraine days in participants who have both conditions. It’s expected to finish in 2031, according to ClinicalTrials.gov.

In a recent development, people who suspect they have both conditions can take steps now to get them treated together, Stuparich said.Patients can raise the connection themselves, Stuparich said. She suggested a starting point for each appointment:.

Recent findings suggest that patients can also ask for an early referral to the other specialist so both conditions get coordinated care, Woldeamanuel mentioned. “The earlier it’s diagnosed, the better it’s managed,” he said.Stuparich said doctors are moving away from viewing endometriosis as only a gynecologic disorder because it can affect the whole body.“It is a whole body systemic neuroinflammatory neuroimmune disorder,” she said.

The best motorcycle gifts don’t have to be flashy. A well-chosen upgrade can make a cold commute more comfortable, a long tour easier to manage, or time in the garage more rewarding. The trick is matching the present to the person: what they ride, where they go, and what gear they already own.

This guide covers a range of options, from protective apparel and useful electronics to compact accessories and garage staples. Whether you’re shopping for a longtime rider or someone still getting used to life on two wheels, you’ll find ideas for different styles, needs, and budgets.

According to recent reports, kriega is the leading brand in motorcycle baggage, and its backpacks are no different. Waterproof inside and with 20 liters of storage space, the R20 backpack is perfect for commuting and features Kreiga's harness-style fasteners. An innovative technology pioneered specifically for motorcycles, the chest clip and straps allow the bag's weight to be pushed forward, making sure that the weight stays centered on the back without disturbing your riding balance.

It's the perfect motorcycling backpack as far as we're concerned.

Give a motorcyclist a gift that makes every ride easier to relive—and can help document the unexpected. The Insta360 X5 Motorcycle Bundle captures 8K 360-degree video, letting riders choose angles later instead of fiddling with framing on the road. FlowState stabilization smooths bumpy footage, while the heavy-duty clamp and invisible selfie stick are ready for bike-mounted shots. It’s a fun way to share adventures and a useful record if a ride takes an unwelcome turn.

This extremely compact starter box is 33% thinner, 27% smaller, and 34% lighter than most portable jump-packs, so it slips right into your pocket. Rated at 1500 amps, it can even jump-start cars, motorcycles, trucks, ATVs, boats, RVs, vans, and SUVs. Best of all, it's equipped with a flashlight and two fast-charging USB ports, both A and C, so it can easily charge your favorite USB devices while it's in your pocket. No motorcyclist should flip up the kickstand without one.

This helmet wall mount is perfect for those who want to save space. It easily mounts on any wall and swivels to display helmets or other items as desired. When not in use, it can be pushed against the wall to take up less space. A bottom hook lets you hang your jacket, keeping all your riding gear together.

It has been revealed that hand signals from your riding buddy can only go so far, especially when a waving arm could mean anything. Communication systems go a long way toward enjoying group rides and Cardo's PackTalk PRO is the perfect communication system for individual and group use. The waterproof model includes a mesh network Bluetooth connection for phone calls, directions, and music while also allowing for rider-to-rider communications. JBL speakers are included in the package and make communications and music crystal clear. Best of all, you can set up voice commands and speed dial to make sure those eyes stay on the road.

Recent findings suggest that few gifts can improve a rider's safety as dramatically as the Brake Free Helmet Light. This clever wireless device mounts to the back of nearly any helmet and uses built-in sensors to detect braking, downshifting, and engine braking, illuminating bright LEDs at eye level for drivers behind you. With no wiring, no apps, and a weatherproof design, it's an easy upgrade that boosts visibility day or night. For riders who value safety without sacrificing simplicity, this is one of the smartest gifts on the road.

For the rider who owns the gloves, jacket, and boots, give them something that matters most when a ride goes wrong: Alpinestars’ Tech-Air 5 Plasma airbag system. This lightweight, breathable vest slips beneath a motorcycle jacket and deploys to protect the chest, ribs, back, and shoulders. It offers STREET, OFF-ROAD, and RACE modes, up to 30 hours of battery life, and a user-replaceable inflator. It’s an investment in safer miles—and a thoughtful gift with purpose. Available in sizes XS-4XL.

Industry observers note that you don't need to be a biker to love this Lego set. It includes a two-speed gearbox and front and rear suspension for realistic movement. The attention to detail is impressive, like the turning handlebar and front and rear disc brakes. A kickstand, exhaust pipe, windshield, and dashboard add the little details that make this model true to the full-size version. Designed in collaboration with Ducati, it's a Technic set, so it's far more than just a toy or model. Still, Lego enthusiasts who want a bigger challenge should try the 1900-piece Technic BMW M 1000 RR ($249.99 at Lego) set.

Quad Lock makes a huge variety of phone-mounting gear, and motorcyclist-specific products are some of the most popular. This particular unit, the Quad Lock Motorcycle Handlebar Mount, includes everything you'll need to install it on any motorcycle and allows for your choice of mounting angle. You'll also need to get one of QuadLock's sleek phone cases to complete the package.

Some riders don't like to wear significant clunky boots. Now they can go straight from the bike to the bar with these comfortable moto-specific riding shoes. They're comfortable and easy to wear, with sturdy construction and strong materials around the toe area. They're available in multiple sizes (tip: Know your EU size to get the best fit) and colors including brown and two-tone.

Affordable with no brand or riding style affiliations, this is the perfect fun gift for those riders who are hard to buy for.

According to recent reports, available in black, gray, and tan (shown), this over-the-shoulder sling bag is perfect for riders who hate wearing backpacks. You can keep your wallet, phone, keys, and other valuables inside and secure while riding. We've used this many times; we barely feel it on us and love the convenience.

Recent findings suggest that if your favorite rider is an ADV fanatic who loves to explore off-road, the Garmin zūmo XT3 is the perfect present. Its ultrabright 4.7-inch display is glove-friendly and rain-resistant. It can withstand all kinds of weather, extreme temperatures, and vibrations. They'll get adventurous routes with turn-by-turn directions and topographic or satellite imagery for off-road guidance. Plus, they can manage and review routes, tracks, and waypoints on their smartphone and computer—no subscription needed.

Perfect for motorcycles, this 750-amp, 12-volt Battery Tender is smarter than a trickle charger because it provides a full charge, then switches to Float mode to keep your battery at an optimal level for safe, long-term storage without overcharging. It's compatible with all 12V lead-acid, flooded, AGM, and gel cell batteries.

Sources indicate that the ultimate motorcycle gift? Ecuador Freedom offers guided and self-guided tours all over one of South America's most beautiful countries, starting at around $2k. Starting in the central capital city of Quito, these multi-day tours can go on- or off-road (or both!), up to colossal Andean peaks or volcanoes (or both!), and down to the Pacific Ocean to the west or the Amazon jungle to the east (or both!) Freedom also rents Jeeps and other 4x4s. The adventure is yours.

Recent findings suggest that four carbon fiber heating elements generate heat across the collar, mid-back, as well as underneath. It features two pockets for core-body warmth and three heat settings for comfort no matter where the ride takes you.

Sources indicate that whether your bike is a tool for metropolitan mobility or rural enjoyment, it's never a bad idea to lock it up when parked. Motorcycle theft is a huge problem in major cities around the world, but a simple disc lock will fend off the majority of thieves. Kryptonite makes it simple with the Keeper Disc Lock, blending hardened materials with affordable pricing. And don't forget to use the orange reminder cable; we know from personal experience that trying to ride away with a disc lock on isn't a pretty sight.

A good balaclava is one of those pieces of riding gear you don't appreciate until you ride without one. The Censgo Motorcycle Balaclava is designed with lightweight, moisture-wicking fabric and breathable mesh panels that help keep riders cool, dry, and comfortable on hot-weather rides. It slips easily under a helmet, reduces sweat buildup, and adds a layer of protection from wind, dust, and bugs. Affordable, practical, and useful on nearly every ride, it's a stocking stuffer any motorcyclist will appreciate.

Recent findings suggest that tired of rolling up those foam earplugs and stuffing them in your ears? Try Earpeace Moto. I was skeptical about these at first, but you get a number of them, along with a handy carrying case. They work as advertised to block out unwanted noise on a long ride, and they don't get your ear canals sore as those foam plugs do after a daylong ride. You can also wear them discreetly at concerts without looking totally uncool. Perfect stocking—or, er, ear canal—stuffer.

Recent findings suggest that every rider knows that tire pressure can make or break a day on the road, which is why the AstroAI L7 Tire Inflator is a smart gift that delivers real-world value. This compact cordless air compressor packs up to 150 PSI, features automatic shutoff to prevent overinflation, and includes a built-in LED light for roadside emergencies. Small enough to stash in a saddlebag yet powerful enough for motorcycles, bicycles, and more, it's the kind of tool riders will actually use.

In a recent development, useful gifts include riding gear, luggage, maintenance tools, navigation devices, communication systems, and small comforts such as insulated drinkware. Think about how the recipient rides: a daily commuter may value weather protection, while a touring rider might appreciate route-planning gear or extra storage.

Industry observers note that check the make, model, and year before buying anything that mounts to or fits the motorcycle. Phone mounts, luggage, covers, and electronics can vary in compatibility. If you can’t confirm the details, choose a universal accessory or a gift card from a motorcycle gear retailer.

According to recent reports, yes, but fit matters. Jackets, gloves, boots, and protective equipment need to fit correctly and suit the rider’s needs. For helmets, ask about the recipient’s preferred brand, size, and model first; a gift card may be a better choice than guessing.

Check the rider’s size and preferred fit, plus the weather and conditions they ride in. Ventilated gear may suit warm-weather riding, while waterproof layers and heated accessories can be welcome for commuting or touring. Look for a gift receipt in case the fit isn’t right.

They can be. Commuters may appreciate rain gear, visibility accessories, or compact storage. Touring riders might get more use from luggage, navigation, communication gear, or comfort upgrades. When in doubt, choose something that works across different kinds of rides.

Absolutely. Riders often have specific preferences about brands, fit, and compatibility. A gift card lets them choose gear that suits their bike and riding style while still giving them something to look forward to.

💡 Key Takeaways
